section: Home Rule Movement - Tilak and Annie Besant; impact
subsections: Home Rule Leagues → founder, year, place, area, merger

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Home Rule Leagues:
1. Tilak's Indian Home Rule League was founded on 28 April 1916.
2. Tilak's League was launched at Belgaum and based at Poona.
3. Besant's All India Home Rule League had its headquarters at Adyar in Madras.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Tilak launched his League at the Belgaum session of the Bombay Provincial Conference on 28 April 1916, with Poona as its base, while Besant's headquarters was at Adyar, Madras.
accepted.tq: Combine closely related date, place and headquarters facts and test whether all statements hold.
accepted.sec: Home Rule Leagues → founder, year, place, area, merger  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Tilak's Indian Home Rule League was founded in which of the following months and years?
accepted.x: Tilak's Indian Home Rule League was founded on 28 April 1916. His release from Mandalay prison in June 1914 preceded the League by nearly two years.
accepted.tq: Use the exact date to distinguish the League from Tilak's earlier self-government activities and imprisonment.
accepted.sec: Home Rule Leagues → founder, year, place, area, merger  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The All India Home Rule League of Annie Besant was founded in:
accepted.x: Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League was founded in Madras in September 1916. Its headquarters was at Adyar, in Gokhale Hall.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two Leagues by separating their founding places and dates.
accepted.sec: Home Rule Leagues → founder, year, place, area, merger  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the territorial jurisdiction of Tilak's Home Rule League?
o: Madras Presidency, Bengal and Assam only
Bombay city, Madras and the Central Provinces
Maharashtra excluding Bombay city, Karnataka, Central Provinces and Berar
The whole of India including Bombay city
accepted.x: Tilak's League operated in Maharashtra except Bombay city, Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar. Besant's League covered the rest of India, including Bombay city.
accepted.tq: Test the reversed-area trap by comparing the territorial spheres of the two Leagues.
accepted.sec: Home Rule Leagues → founder, year, place, area, merger  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Home Rule Leagues, consider the following statements:
1. Besant's League covered the rest of India, including Bombay city.
2. Besant's League had approximately 200 branches.
3. Tilak's League reached a wider audience than Besant's League.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Besant's League covered the rest of India and had about 200 branches, while Tilak's League was better organised but Besant's League reached a wider audience.
accepted.tq: Identify the reversed comparison in statement 3 while retaining the correct geographical and numerical statements.
accepted.sec: Home Rule Leagues → founder, year, place, area, merger  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Office-bearer)
a. Joseph Baptista
b. N.C. Kelkar
c. George Arundale
d. B.P. Wadia

List-II (Association)
i. Secretary of Tilak's League
ii. President of Tilak's League

accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair of Joseph Baptista with Tilak's League and complete the matching.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the subsequent history of the Home Rule Leagues is correct?
o: Their work merged into Besant's All India Home Rule League, which was renamed Swarajya Sabha in 1920 under Gandhi's presidency.
The two Leagues were merged into Tilak's League in 1918.
Besant's League was renamed Swarajya Sabha in 1916 under Jinnah's presidency.
Both Leagues remained separate until the end of the freedom movement.
accepted.x: The work of the two Leagues later merged into Besant's All India Home Rule League. In 1920 it was renamed Swarajya Sabha under Mahatma Gandhi's presidency.
accepted.tq: Use the merger and renaming sequence to reject swapped leadership and dates.
accepted.sec: Home Rule Leagues → founder, year, place, area, merger  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Tilak's Home Rule League?
o: It was founded by Tilak in 1914 immediately after his release from Mandalay jail.
accepted.x: The statement is NOT correct because Tilak's League was founded in April 1916, not in 1914. Tilak was released from Mandalay jail on 16 June 1914.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong year in the statement while retaining its correct founder and associated place.
accepted.sec: Home Rule Leagues → founder, year, place, area, merger  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who popularised the Home Rule idea in the United Provinces and is associated with the statement, “First we are Indians, then only Muslims”?
accepted.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah popularised the Home Rule movement in the United Provinces. The statement emphasised a common Indian political identity above communal distinctions.
accepted.tq: Link the quotation to the leader's specific regional role in the movement.
accepted.sec: Home Rule Leagues → founder, year, place, area, merger  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Commonweal, founded by Annie Besant, was a:
accepted.x: Commonweal was an English weekly founded by Annie Besant in January 1914. It was one of the important newspapers through which she propagated political ideas.
accepted.tq: Combine the paper's founder, language and date to distinguish it from Besant's New India.

accepted.s: Annie Besant renamed the Madras Standard as New India after purchasing it in:
accepted.x: Annie Besant purchased the Madras Standard in July 1914 and renamed it New India. New India was a daily newspaper.
accepted.tq: Use the exact month and the newspaper's earlier name as the discriminating clues.

accepted.s: The Government demanded a security of Rs. 2,000 from Commonweal and New India under the Press Act and subsequently demanded an additional amount of:
accepted.x: After demanding Rs. 2,000 as security and confiscating it, the Government demanded a further Rs. 10,000. Annie Besant paid the amount to continue the newspapers.
accepted.tq: Track the two-stage monetary demand instead of confusing the initial security with the later demand.

accepted.s: The first Indian woman to preside over the Indian National Congress was:
accepted.x: Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President of the Congress. She presided over the Kanpur session in 1925.
accepted.tq: Separate nationality from gender by comparing the first woman president with the first Indian woman president.

accepted.s: Nellie Sengupta presided over which session of the Indian National Congress?
accepted.x: Nellie Sengupta presided over the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1933 and was the third woman president listed in this sequence.
accepted.tq: Use the session-place and year pair to distinguish successive women presidents.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Annie Besant presides over the Calcutta session of the INC
B. Sarojini Naidu presides over the Kanpur session of the INC
C. Nellie Sengupta presides over the Calcutta session of the INC

Choose the correct answer:
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Annie Besant in 1917, Sarojini Naidu in 1925 and Nellie Sengupta in 1933.
accepted.tq: Arrange the events by their years before checking the session locations.

accepted.s: Annie Besant was styled as the:
accepted.x: Annie Besant was styled the “Iron Lady of Ireland.” She was of Irish origin and later became a prominent Indian nationalist leader.
accepted.tq: Test the title-person association without confusing Besant's title with titles associated with Indian leaders.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Tilak's newspapers is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Tilak founded or edited Kesari as a Marathi paper and Mahratta as an English paper; both are associated with the year 1881.
accepted.tq: Use the language distinction between two newspapers with the same founder and year.

accepted.s: Tilak began the public celebration of Ganeshotsav and the Shivaji festival respectively in:
accepted.x: Tilak began the public Ganeshotsav celebration in 1893 and the Shivaji festival in 1895. Both festivals were used to promote public mobilisation and nationalist consciousness.
accepted.tq: Remember the paired years in sequence and reject the reversed-order option.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly conveys Tilak's observation on the Lucknow Pact?
o: “Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers.”
“First we are Indians, then only Muslims.”
“Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.”
“The British Empire is rotten to the core.”
accepted.x: Tilak described the Lucknow Pact in the words, “Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers.” The other statements are associated with different contexts or speakers.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among famous nationalist quotations by matching each statement with its context.
